_about: Golden cases for when a disappearing message's countdown starts and when the message is deleted.
The wire halves are pinned elsewhere: a message's own timer is `x` in payload.json, and the conversation's timer is `dis` in group-meta.json.
`maxSeconds` is the longest timer, 2,419,200 seconds (four weeks).

Each `expiry` case: every time is unix milliseconds. `outgoing` is whether the viewer wrote the message, on any of their devices. `timer` is the message's `x`. `sentAt` is the message's own time. `readAt` is when this device first showed it in an open, attended transcript (null: not yet). `noteAt` is the time of a read note from another of the viewer's devices (null: none). `now` is the clock.
`startedAt` is when the countdown started (null: not started) and `expiresAt` when the message is deleted (null: not scheduled).
To replay: run each case through your own implementation of the format and compare the result with the case's expectation, field by field.

expiry.name: an outgoing message starts when it was sent
an incoming message not yet read has not started
an incoming message starts when this device showed it
another device of mine read it first: its note's time
a note stamped in the future is clamped to now
the earlier of this device's read and the note wins
a message with no timer never starts
